title: Can ChatGPT Forecast Stock Price Movements? Return Predictability and Large Language Models

task.value: Test whether off-the-shelf LLMs like ChatGPT can predict stock market reactions (initial reaction and subsequent drift) from firm news headlines.
task.quote: We document the capability of large language models (LLMs) like ChatGPT to predict stock market reactions from news headlines without direct financial training.

architecture.value: Zero-shot prompting: GPT-4 acts as a financial expert, answers YES/NO/UNKNOWN per headline (mapped to 1/-1/0), temperature 0; scores form daily-rebalanced equal-weighted long-short portfolios and regressions.
architecture.quote: We transform it into a numerical ‘‘GPT-4 score,” where ‘‘YES” is mapped to 1, ‘‘UNKNOWN” to 0, and ‘‘NO” to -1.

data.value: CRSP daily returns, web-scraped news headlines matched to RavenPack, and TAQ intraday data; 159,137 firm-headline-date observations covering 4,123 U.S. common stocks (NYSE, NASDAQ, AMEX); daily and intraday frequency.
data.quote: our final sample comprises 159,137 firm-headline-date observations covering 4,123 unique companies from October 2021 to May 2024, representing about 85% of the 4,875 firms in CRSP during this period.

window.value: October 2021 to May 2024, after the GPT-4 training cutoff (September 2021); no training for GPT-4. Embedding baselines use rolling 6-month training windows retrained monthly after a 9-month warm-up.
window.quote: The sample period begins in October 2021 and ends in May 2024. This sample period ensures that our evaluation is out-of-sample as the training data of the ChatGPT models stops in September 2021

models.value: GPT-4 (gpt-4-0314) main; also GPT-3.5 (gpt-3.5-turbo-0301), GPT-1, GPT-2, BERT, BERT-Large, BART-Large, DistilBart-MNLI-12-1, FinBERT, Llama2 7B/13B/70B; embeddings text-embedding-ada-002 and all-MiniLM-L6-v2.
models.quote: We use the ChatGPT model version ‘‘gpt-4-0314” whose training data stops in September 2021 to ensure that our analysis is an out-of-sample evaluation.

baselines.value: Other LLMs of varying size, FinBERT, RavenPack sentiment scores, supervised embedding models (OpenAI, MiniLM) with logistic regression, and a value-weighted market portfolio.
baselines.quote: We compare GPT-4 against three alternative approaches: (i) domain-specific models trained on financial text (FinBERT), (ii) supervised learning models trained on actual return outcomes (embeddings), and (iii) LLMs of varying complexity.

headline_result.value: GPT-4 long-short: 93.3% (88.8%) hit rate on initial reaction for overnight (intraday) news; drift strategy 0.34% mean daily return, annualized Sharpe 2.97 (overnight) before costs, Oct 2021–May 2024.
headline_result.quote: These drift strategies achieve annualized pre-transaction-costs Sharpe ratios of 2.97 for overnight news and 2.63 for intraday news.

costs.value: Fixed round-trip costs of 5, 10, 20 bps; cumulative return over 300% at 5 bps, above 100% at 10 bps, unprofitable at 20 bps. Sharpe falls to 1.29 at 10 bps (100% rebalancing).
costs.quote: Assuming a transaction cost of 5 bps round-trip, the strategy still earns a cumulative return of over 300% during our sample period. As we increase the transaction costs to 10 bps round-trip, the cumulative return is still above 100%. A transaction cost of 20 bps round-trip makes the strategy unprofitable.

uncertainty.value: Regressions with firm and date fixed effects and standard errors double-clustered by date and firm (t-stats reported); 95% confidence intervals on event-time returns and yearly Sharpe ratios; temperature 0 for reproducibility.
uncertainty.quote: Standard errors are double-clustered by date and firm.

leakage_controls.value: Sample restricted to post-September 2021 knowledge cutoff; GPT-4 vs GPT-3.5 advantage over time checked (increases, inconsistent with memorization); Llama2 cutoff later noted as possible overstatement.
leakage_controls.quote: We further address potential lookahead bias concerns by comparing GPT-4 to GPT-3.5 performance over time in Online Appendix C. GPT-4 performs better in the latter part of the sample, inconsistent with the model having knowledge outside of its cutoff date.

limitations.value: Exploitable only for low-cost traders; predictability concentrated in small stocks; GPT parameter counts unconfirmed; Llama2 results may be overstated; decline in Sharpe may reflect other factors; news sample skews larger firms.
limitations.quote: However, exploiting these patterns in practice is only feasible for market participants whose transaction costs are sufficiently low, such as market makers.
